criteria.quote: Poliwag swims well, yet fast rivers make it cling.
criteria.revision: Open with the contradiction as a question: “Swimming is easier than walking—so why does Poliwag cling to a rock in fast-flowing water?”

criteria.quote: In fast-flowing rivers, Poliwag clings to rocks because its thick lips act like suction cups.
If swimming is easier, why cling to a rock?
criteria.revision: Keep this as the opening question, but delay the explanation until the final reveal instead of repeating the answer in the premise and payoff.

criteria.quote: In fast-flowing rivers, Poliwag clings to a rock instead.
criteria.revision: Build in three distinct steps: establish that swimming is easier than walking, introduce the fast-flowing-river rock cling, then reveal that its thick lips act like a suction cup. Remove the separate “current keeps flowing” beat because it does not raise the stakes.

criteria.quote: Poliwag’s Lips Work Like Suction Cups
criteria.revision: Hide the mechanism from the title and opening. Use a curiosity title such as “Why Does Poliwag Cling to Rocks?” and reserve “its thick lips act like a suction cup” for the late reveal.

criteria.quote: Poliwag swims well, yet fast rivers make it cling.
criteria.revision: Combine the first and third scenes, since both establish that Poliwag clings in fast-flowing water. Cut or replace “The current keeps flowing, but Poliwag keeps clinging to the rock,” which repeats the same fact without adding new information.

criteria.quote: Its thick lips act like a suction cup, letting Poliwag cling to a rock in fast-flowing water.
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve the contradiction directly: “Swimming is easier than walking—but in fast-flowing rivers, Poliwag’s thick lips act like a suction cup so it can cling to a rock.”

criteria.quote: Better river move: suction-cup lips or swimming?
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported “better” comparison with an evidence-grounded split: “Which is stranger: that Poliwag is better at swimming than walking, or that its thick lips act like a suction cup when it clings to rocks?”
